Ted wrote in ISAIF that he divided human drives into three groups:
1. Drives which can be satisfied with minimal effort
2. Drives which can be satisfied only at the cost of the maximum effort
3. Drives which can't be satisified regardless of the degree of the effort

He also wrote that the power process refers to satisfying the drives of the second group, and that, due to the limited autonomy in the industrial society, most of the drives now belong either in the first group (food, water, entertainment, sex etc) or the third group (freedom, self-sufficency, independence from the system etc), both of which lead to frustration, low self-esteem and depression.

Tl;dr Yes, that absolutely explains the suicide rates. Pic related.
